name: Kimya (ARMOR Group)
summary: French engineering-filament brand of the ARMOR Group industrial group, positioned for functional end-use parts rather than hobbyist printing. Best documented product is ABS-R, an impact-modified ABS; the broader catalog reportedly spans PLA, PETG, TPU, nylon (including reinforced grades), PC and carbon/glass-fiber-filled engineering materials.

oem_relationships.notes: Kimya is described across distributor listings as ARMOR Group's 3D-printing materials brand ('Kimya 3D printing filament by Armor Group'), i.e. an in-house brand rather than a reseller. Recorded as 'joint-venture' because the enum has no parent-company value; this is corporate ownership, not a supply relationship. Note that ARMOR's own corporate site division list (ARMOR-IIMAK, ARMOR Battery Films, ALTKIN) did not show Kimya as a current named division, so the ownership may have changed — see provenance.conflicts. Not present in research/verified-oem-relationships.md.

product_lines.name: ABS-R
product_lines.notes: Recycled-content, impact-modified ABS. Sample price $22.65 for a black spool at MatterHackers.

product_lines.name: ABS-EC
product_lines.notes: ABS grade engineered for larger and more complex parts.

product_lines.name: ABS Kevlar
product_lines.notes: ABS reinforced with aramid (Kevlar) fiber - an unusual filler with no carbon/glass equivalent id in this catalog.

product_lines.name: ABS-ESD
product_lines.notes: ABS doped with conductive filler for static-dissipative use. No abs-esd id exists (only petg-esd).

product_lines.name: ABS Carbon / ABS Carbon Black
product_lines.notes: ABS + carbon fiber, sold partly through the Raise3D partner channel. No abs-cf id exists in this catalog.

product_lines.name: PETG-R
product_lines.notes: Recycled PETG made from post-consumer packaging waste.

product_lines.name: PA6-CO
product_lines.notes: Carbon-filled polyamide 6. Kimya does not separate fiber loading from black pigment in the listings found, so the -cf mapping rests on the product's reinforced positioning rather than a stated fiber %.

product_lines.name: PEKK Semicrystalline
product_lines.notes: Semicrystalline-processed PEKK: higher HDT and different post-processing than the amorphous grade, same polymer.

product_lines.name: PEKK Carbon
product_lines.notes: PEKK + carbon fiber. No pekk-cf id exists in this catalog.

product_lines.name: PEBA-S
product_lines.notes: Pebax-type polyether-block-amide thermoplastic elastomer - higher rebound and lower compression set than TPU at comparable hardness, and chemically distinct from it. No peba id exists.

additional_notes: This entry rests largely on distributor listings: kimya.fr could not be fetched in this research session (robots/SSL blocks), so the website endpoint is the believed URL with unverified reachability, and filament2print's Kimya brand page returned 404. The product line list beyond ABS-R is industry-standard-knowledge rather than sourced itemisation. Whether Kimya's filament is extruded at ARMOR's Nantes HQ site (20 rue Chevreul, 44105 Nantes) or a separate ARMOR facility is unverified; manufacturing_countries is set to France on brand positioning and ARMOR's French base rather than a confirmed plant. Build-plate products not confirmed either way, so makes_plates is left unset. No social profiles confirmed. Price tier is recorded as engineering on positioning ('functional end-use parts'), though the one confirmed price point sits in mid territory. UPDATE (trade-name pass): the product line list is no longer inferred - it is now itemised from kimya.fr category/product pages plus the 3DGBIRE and Raise3D partner catalogs. Kimya's own site is partly protected by anti-bot measures, so the list is thorough but not guaranteed exhaustive at the colour/SKU level. The previously-listed TPU, PC, PA-GF and generic 'nylon' lines were removed because no source in this pass supports them; PEBA-S is Kimya's flexible offering.

provenance.conflicts: Corporate structure is genuinely unresolved: older sources and current distributor copy describe Kimya as an ARMOR Group brand, but ARMOR's own site division list (ARMOR-IIMAK, ARMOR Battery Films, ALTKIN) does not name Kimya — so Kimya may have been divested, renamed or restructured out of ARMOR. Could not be settled in this research session; flagged for follow-up. Secondary gaps: no Kimya-controlled source was reachable, so the product range beyond ABS-R, the manufacturing site and the official URL are all unverified.
